_comment: The scope table slack_manifest.py builds every tier from and validates every manifest against.
One row per scope: the scope, the token types Slack's own reference page lists for it, the
LOWEST tier that requests it (tiers are cumulative: minimal is inside standard, standard is
inside full; null means no tier requests it), a one-line why, and the page that says so.
Source and date: every row was checked against Slack's official developer reference on
2026-11-06, reading the token_types field of each scope page's markdown twin,
https://docs.slack.dev/reference/scopes/<scope>.md, where <scope> is the scope name with
':' written as '.' (channels:read -> channels.read). The `source` column is the same URL
without '.md'. A scope missing from this table is REFUSED by the validator, whether it is
invented or real-but-unvetted: adding one means opening its page, copying its token types
and writing its why here.
A row whose token_types lacks "Bot" is an ability Slack grants only to a USER token (a
token acting as the person who installed the app), and the admin.* rows additionally
need an Enterprise plan and an org-wide install by an org admin or owner
(https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/admin.conversations.create). No tier requests one:
they are listed so the person choosing a tier sees what a bot token cannot do, and so the
validator can refuse one placed in oauth_config.scopes.bot with that reason rather than as
an unknown scope.
"Legacy Bot" is the bot of a classic Slack app. A manifest's scopes.bot is the granular
bot token, which is "Bot" and only "Bot".

scopes.why: List the public channels the bot was invited to (users.conversations): how the watcher finds what to poll.
The same for private channels the bot was invited to.
Read messages and thread replies in those public channels (conversations.history, conversations.replies).
The same for those private channels.
Post and reply in threads as the bot, and edit or delete its own messages (chat.postMessage, chat.update, chat.delete).
Find the direct-message conversations people opened with the bot (users.conversations with types=im).
Read those direct messages; the watcher polls them, so no Events API subscription is needed.
Open a direct message with a person first (conversations.open), for example to chase a blocker.
Acknowledge a message with an emoji reaction (reactions.add, reactions.remove).
See the reactions on a message (reactions.get), such as an approval given by emoji.
Upload screenshots, logs and other artifacts (files.getUploadURLExternal, files.completeUploadExternal).
Fetch the files people attach in its channels and direct messages (files.info).
Resolve a user id to a name and time zone (users.info, users.list) for a sender it has no label for.
Read profile fields such as title and status (users.profile.get) when deciding whom to address.
Create, rename, archive and unarchive public channels, set topic and purpose, invite and remove members (conversations.create, .archive, .rename, .invite, .kick).
The same for private channels it was added to, and create new private channels.
Join a public channel by itself (conversations.join); without it a person's invite is the only way in, and every channel it joins reaches its session.
Post in a public channel it is not a member of, for announcements; posting this way does not subscribe it to the channel.
List user groups and their members (usergroups.list, usergroups.users.list).
Create, update, enable and disable user groups and set their members (usergroups.create, usergroups.users.update); paid plans only.
List what is pinned in a channel (pins.list).
Pin and unpin messages (pins.add, pins.remove).
List a channel's bookmarks (bookmarks.list).
Add, edit and remove channel bookmarks (bookmarks.add, bookmarks.edit, bookmarks.remove).
Find a member by e-mail address (users.lookupByEmail), for example before inviting them to a channel.
Read the workspace's name, domain and icon (team.info).
Read the workspace's preferences (team.preferences.list), so it can tell a refused action from a broken one.
Approve or decline Slack Connect invitations and manage external-organization connections (conversations.approveSharedInvite); paid plans only.
Invite an external organization into a channel it is in, and accept invitations sent to it (conversations.inviteShared, conversations.acceptSharedInvite).
Invite people into the workspace, deactivate or remove members, make someone an admin or owner, reset sessions (admin.users.invite, .remove, .setAdmin). User token, Enterprise plan.
List members with their admin-level details and sessions (admin.users.list). User token, Enterprise plan.
Approve or deny requests to invite people into the workspace (admin.inviteRequests.approve). User token, Enterprise plan.

Delete a channel, convert it between public and private, make it org-wide or move it between workspaces, archive channels it is not in (admin.conversations.delete, .convertToPrivate). User token, Enterprise plan.
Look up and read the settings of every channel, including ones it is not in (admin.conversations.lookup). User token, Enterprise plan.
Tie user groups to channels and workspaces as defaults (admin.usergroups.addChannels). User token, Enterprise plan.
Change the workspace's name, icon, description, discoverability and default channels, and add or remove custom emoji (admin.teams.settings.setName, admin.emoji.add). User token, Enterprise plan.
Delete, restore or edit any member's message (oversight.chat.delete). User token, Enterprise plan.
Assign and remove admin roles (admin.roles.addAssignments). User token, Enterprise plan.
Approve or restrict the apps members may install (admin.apps.approve). User token, Enterprise plan.
Read the workspace's access logs, billable-member info and integration logs (team.accessLogs, team.billableInfo, team.integrationLogs). User token only.
Read the Audit Logs API. User token, Enterprise organizations only, installed by the organization's owner.
Manage public channels on a person's behalf. User token only; the bot equivalent is channels:manage, which the full tier requests.
Edit a member's profile and status (users.profile.set). User token only, and another member's profile only by an admin on a paid plan.
Search messages and files across the workspace (search.messages, search.all). User token only.
